title: Will the official USD to ARS exchange rate be between 1900.00 and 1999.99 at the end of December 2026?

forecast.rationale: Argentina’s official USD/ARS rate is highly policy-dependent, with risks of step devaluations, changes to crawling-peg rules, or exchange-rate unification before end-2026. A rate in the 1900–1999.99 band is plausible under a moderate crawling-depreciation path from 2024–2026, but the band is narrow relative to Argentina’s macro and policy uncertainty.

title: Canada recession before 2027?

forecast.rationale: Canada faces elevated recession risk from high household debt, housing sensitivity, and exposure to potential U.S. demand/trade shocks, but easing inflation and likely/ongoing monetary policy support reduce the odds of a downturn. With less than a year remaining before 2027, a recession is plausible but not the base case unless labor markets or exports deteriorate materially.

title: Will the Eurozone's 2026 Annual Inflation be between 1.9% and 2.1%?

forecast.rationale: Eurozone inflation is structurally anchored near the ECB’s 2% target, and medium-term forecasts for 2026 have generally clustered around 1.9–2.0%. However, the resolution band is narrow, and annual inflation can be shifted meaningfully by energy prices, exchange rates, wages, or growth surprises, so the miss probability remains slightly higher than the hit probability.

title: Will Canada have the highest unemployment rate since 2016 this year?

forecast.rationale: Canada’s unemployment rate has risen from post-pandemic lows and was around the high-6% range by 2025, making a further increase in 2026 plausible if growth weakens. However, if the benchmark includes the pandemic-era spike in 2020-2021, the bar is very high; even under a mild recession, reaching those levels is unlikely. Overall, the market wording is somewhat ambiguous, but I assign a moderate chance to a 2026 high relative to the non-pandemic post-2016 period and a lower chance if strictly compared to all years since 2016.

title: Will Trump cut corporate taxes before 2027?

forecast.rationale: If Trump is in office with sufficient congressional support, a tax package before the end of 2026 is plausible, especially around expiring TCJA provisions and business-friendly measures. However, a headline corporate rate cut is fiscally costly and may face deficit and legislative constraints, so the outcome depends heavily on how broadly the market interprets “cut corporate taxes.”

title: Fed Rate Hike by April 2026 Meeting?

forecast.rationale: A Fed rate hike by the April 2026 meeting would require a significant inflation resurgence or policy shock strong enough to reverse the easing/holding bias expected after the 2022-24 tightening cycle. The more likely path is cuts or extended holds rather than hikes, though persistent inflation risk leaves a non-trivial tail probability.

US defaults on debt by 2027?

forecast.rationale: An outright U.S. federal debt default before the end of 2026 remains unlikely because Congress has strong incentives to avoid missed Treasury payments and has historically resolved debt-ceiling standoffs before default. However, political polarization and debt-ceiling brinkmanship create a small but non-negligible risk of a technical missed or delayed payment.

title: Will ground beef hit $8 per pound in 2026?

forecast.rationale: Ground beef prices are supported by tight U.S. cattle supplies and elevated beef input costs, making further increases plausible through 2026. However, reaching $8/lb on a broad national retail measure would require a historically large additional rise from recent levels, so it remains more likely not to occur before the close.

title: United x American Airlines merger/acquisition announced in 2026?

forecast.rationale: A United-American merger or acquisition would face extreme U.S. antitrust and DOT scrutiny because it would combine two of the largest domestic carriers and substantially reduce competition on many routes. There is no strong strategic or financial catalyst suggesting either company would pursue such a highly risky deal before the end of 2026.

title: Will the Fed’s lower bound reach 2.75% or lower before 2027?
Will Eurozone annual GDP growth in 2026 be between 4.0% and 5.0%?

forecast.rationale: Eurozone real GDP growth forecasts for 2026 are generally around 1–2%, well below the 4.0% to 5.0% range. Reaching that range would likely require an unusually strong boom or major rebound comparable to post-pandemic conditions, which appears unlikely under current macroeconomic expectations.

title: Will Trump reduce the deficit before 2027?

forecast.rationale: US deficits are structurally elevated due to interest costs, entitlement spending, and likely tax-cut extensions, making a clear reduction before 2027 difficult. Some deficit narrowing is possible from tariffs, spending restraint, or stronger-than-expected revenues, but baseline fiscal dynamics point against a meaningful reduction by the deadline.

title: Will the US economy have slack at the end of 2026?

forecast.rationale: By end-2026, whether the US economy has slack will likely hinge on whether growth has slowed enough to push unemployment above its longer-run sustainable rate or output below potential. Baseline projections around mid-decade have generally implied only modest cooling rather than a deep downturn, but the cumulative risk of recession or below-trend growth before then is meaningful.

title: ECB rate hike in 2026?

forecast.rationale: The ECB is more likely to be in a hold-or-ease stance through 2026 if inflation remains near target and euro-area growth is modest. A hike is still plausible if wage pressures, fiscal stimulus, or an energy shock reignite inflation, but that is not the base case.

title: EU debt downgrade before 2027?

forecast.rationale: EU debt is rated very highly by major agencies and, absent a negative outlook or acute member-state funding crisis, downgrades over a short horizon are relatively uncommon. Rising EU borrowing, fiscal pressures, and political fragmentation create some risk, but the base case is ratings stability through the end of 2026.

title: US recession by end of 2026?

forecast.rationale: The U.S. economy has shown resilience, and absent a clear current downturn, a soft-landing/no-recession outcome remains more likely. However, recession risk through end-2026 is still material given the lagged effects of tight monetary policy, potential labor-market weakening, and vulnerability to policy or financial shocks.

title: Will inflation reach more than 4% in 2026?

forecast.rationale: Assuming this refers to headline year-over-year CPI inflation in a major economy such as the U.S., baseline forecasts generally point to inflation staying near 2–3% rather than reaccelerating above 4%. However, the threshold could be reached if there are renewed energy shocks, tariff/supply-chain pressures, or unexpectedly strong demand, so the risk is meaningful but below even odds.

title: ECB rate cut in 2026?

forecast.rationale: The ECB had already moved substantially toward a lower-rate stance by the mid-2020s, making further cuts in 2026 possible but not assured if inflation remains near target. Given several policy meetings remain before year-end and euro-area growth risks could justify easing, I assign a modestly above-even chance of at least one 2026 cut.

UK Recession in 2026?

title: Will Mexico’s 2026 Annual Inflation be between 3.00% and 3.49%?

forecast.rationale: Mexico’s inflation is likely to be near Banxico’s 3% target by late 2026, but expectations have tended to remain somewhat above target and shocks to food, energy, FX, or administered prices are common. A 3.00%–3.49% outcome is plausible but narrow, with meaningful probability that inflation is either still above 3.5% or undershoots below 3%.

title: Will no Fed rate cuts happen in 2026?
Japan recession in 2026?

forecast.rationale: Japan’s trend growth is low and its economy is vulnerable to external demand shocks, yen/import-price pressures, and policy tightening, so the risk of a technical recession in any given year is meaningful. However, absent clear evidence of a major global downturn, baseline expectations favor weak but positive growth rather than two consecutive quarters of contraction in 2026.

title: Will India’s 2026 Annual Inflation be between 2.25% and 2.99%?

forecast.rationale: India's CPI inflation is structurally and policy-wise centered near the RBI's 4% target, with most medium-term forecasts for 2026 closer to 4% than to below 3%. A 2.25%–2.99% annual inflation outcome would likely require unusually benign food and energy prices and weak price pressures, making it possible but relatively unlikely.

title: Christine Lagarde out as ECB president in 2026?

forecast.rationale: Christine Lagarde’s ECB term runs until October 2027, so she is expected to still be president throughout 2026 absent an early resignation, removal, incapacity, or death. Such early departures from top central bank roles are uncommon, though not impossible given age, political opportunities, or unforeseen personal circumstances.

title: Negative GDP growth in 2026?

forecast.rationale: Negative full-year GDP growth in 2026 would likely require a recession or several weak quarters, while baseline forecasts generally imply modest positive growth. Downside risks remain from tight financial conditions, policy uncertainty, and external shocks, but the hurdle for an annual contraction is relatively high.

title: Will China's annual inflation in 2026 be less than -1.0%?

forecast.rationale: China has been experiencing very low inflation and intermittent CPI deflation, reflecting weak domestic demand and property-sector drag. However, an annual CPI decline below -1.0% would be unusually deep by recent historical standards, and policy easing or food/energy volatility would likely keep the full-year average closer to zero than materially negative.

title: Will the upper bound of the target federal funds rate be ≥ 4.5% at the end of 2026?

forecast.rationale: The Fed’s long-run neutral-rate estimates and typical market expectations imply further normalization below a 4.5% upper bound by late 2026 if inflation continues to ease. However, sticky inflation, stronger growth, or a renewed inflation shock could keep policy restrictive, so the probability is meaningfully above a tail risk but still below even odds.

title: Will the 2026 trade deficit be less than 500B?

forecast.rationale: Assuming this refers to the U.S. annual goods-and-services trade deficit, recent deficits have been far above $500B, with 2023–2025 levels roughly in the $700B–$900B+ range. Even with tariffs or slower growth, getting below $500B by 2026 would likely require a major recession, large import collapse, or unusual statistical/policy shift, so the threshold looks unlikely to be met.

title: Will Canada’s 2026 inflation be between 3.0% and 3.4%?

forecast.rationale: Canada’s inflation is currently expected by the Bank of Canada and consensus forecasts to be near the 2% target in 2026, making a 3.0%–3.4% annual outcome above the central forecast. However, upside risks from energy prices, currency weakness, tariffs, or supply shocks make this range plausible but not the base case.

title: Fed rate hike in 2026?

forecast.rationale: A 2026 Fed rate hike would likely require a renewed inflation acceleration or a clear overheating signal strong enough to reverse the expected easing/hold bias. Given the Fed’s typical caution after a cutting cycle and the baseline expectation of stable-to-lower rates, a hike before the December 2026 close appears possible but not the central case.

title: Will US GDP growth in 2026 be between 0.5% and 1.0%?

forecast.rationale: US real GDP growth is typically expected to run closer to 1.5%–2.5% absent a recession, making the narrow 0.5%–1.0% band a relatively specific downside outcome. A mild slowdown could put 2026 growth in this range, but the probability mass is larger both above 1.0% and, in a recession scenario, below 0.5%.

title: Will South African inflation be between 4.4% and 4.7% in 2026?

forecast.rationale: South African inflation is likely to remain within the SARB target band in 2026, with many baseline forecasts clustering near the 4%–5% area. However, the specified 4.4%–4.7% range is fairly narrow, and outcomes could easily fall below it if disinflation persists or above it due to rand, fuel, food, or administered-price shocks.

title: Fed emergency rate cut before 2027?

forecast.rationale: An emergency Fed rate cut would likely require a sudden financial crisis or severe recessionary shock, since the FOMC can normally adjust policy at scheduled meetings. Such intermeeting cuts are rare historically, but the nonzero risk over the remaining 2026 horizon comes from potential market stress, banking issues, or a sharp growth downturn.

title: Another US debt downgrade before 2027?
Will Brazil’s Annual Inflation in 2026 be between 3.50% and 3.99%?

title: Will Judy Shelton be confirmed as Fed Chair?

Even under a Republican administration, there are more conventional and confirmable candidates, so the chance she is nominated and confirmed before the deadline appears very low.

title: Will the U.S. national debt hit $40 trillion before 2027?

forecast.rationale: U.S. gross federal debt was already in the mid-$30 trillions by 2024 and has recently been rising by roughly $1.5–2.5 trillion per year amid large deficits and high interest costs. On that trajectory, reaching $40 trillion sometime in 2026 is more likely than not, though timing uncertainty, debt-limit dynamics, and deficit variation leave a meaningful chance it slips past the close time.

title: Will South Korea’s 2026 Annual Inflation be at least 3.0%?

title: Jerome Powell out from Fed Board by May 30?

forecast.rationale: Powell's term as Fed Chair ends in mid-May 2026, while his underlying Fed Board term runs until 2028. Historically, Fed chairs usually leave the Board when replaced, but given the political stakes and his legal ability to remain, there is a meaningful chance he stays at least past May 30.

title: Will world GDP growth be ≤2.9% in 2026?

forecast.rationale: Baseline global growth is typically near 3% and recent institutional forecasts have generally clustered around roughly that level, making 2.9% a close threshold rather than a tail outcome. A mild global slowdown, tighter financial conditions, China/Europe weakness, or geopolitical shocks could push 2026 growth at or below 2.9%, but absent a broad recession the base case is modestly above it.

title: Will the UK’s 2026 inflation be at least 4.5%?

title: Will Trump try to fire Powell as Fed Board Member by December 31, 2026?

forecast.rationale: Trump has strong incentives and a history of attacking Powell, but actually attempting to remove him as a Fed governor would face major legal and market constraints. Powell’s chair term ends in 2026 and he may leave the Board voluntarily or simply be replaced as chair, reducing the need for a direct firing attempt.

title: Will UK annual GDP growth in 2026 be between 4% and 5%?

forecast.rationale: UK real GDP growth for 2026 is currently expected to be near trend, roughly in the 1–2% range, with persistent productivity and fiscal constraints limiting upside. A 4–5% annual expansion would require an unusually strong boom or rebound from a shock, which is possible but unlikely in a mature economy absent a major one-off recovery effect.

title: Will Argentina’s annual inflation be less than 20%?

forecast.rationale: Argentina has made substantial disinflation progress under tight fiscal and monetary policy, and a sub-20% annual CPI rate by 2026 is plausible if stabilization holds. However, getting below 20% requires sustained monthly inflation near or below 1.5%, and Argentina still faces sizable exchange-rate, wage, political, and credibility risks that could keep inflation above that threshold.

title: Fed abolished before 2027?

forecast.rationale: Abolishing the Federal Reserve before the end of 2026 would require sweeping federal legislation and a major restructuring of U.S. monetary and banking institutions. Despite periodic political criticism of the Fed, there is no broad congressional or institutional support for eliminating it on such a short timeline.

title: Costco increases hotdog price before 2027?

forecast.rationale: Costco’s $1.50 hot dog combo is a highly publicized loss-leader and brand symbol, and management has repeatedly signaled strong reluctance to raise the price despite inflation. With the close date before 2027, the remaining window is limited, making a price increase possible but unlikely.

title: Jerome Powell in jail before 2027?

Political pressure or legal disputes involving the Fed could create headlines, but actual jail detention remains highly unlikely over the remaining timeframe.

title: Will the US confirm that aliens exist before Kevin Warsh is confirmed as Fed Chair?

forecast.rationale: A formal U.S. government confirmation that extraterrestrial aliens exist by October 2026 is extremely unlikely, regardless of the Fed chair timeline. Kevin Warsh being confirmed as Fed Chair is itself uncertain, but the alien-confirmation leg is the dominant bottleneck, making a Yes resolution very remote.

title: Will 60 or more of senators vote “Yea” for Trump’s Fed Chair nominee?

forecast.rationale: Fed Chair confirmations often attract some bipartisan support, and with a 53-seat Republican Senate a credible Trump nominee would need only about seven Democratic or independent votes to reach 60. However, confirmations no longer require 60 votes and Democrats may oppose a nominee seen as too politically aligned with Trump, making a sub-60 confirmation plausible even if the nominee is approved.

title: Bank of England rate hike in 2026?

forecast.rationale: The base case is that the Bank of England is more likely to be in a holding or gradual easing phase during 2026 after the post-2022 inflation tightening cycle. A rate hike remains plausible if UK inflation or wage growth reaccelerates, but it is not the central expectation.

title: Will the U.S. 30-year Fixed-Rate Mortgage hit 5.70% (LOW) by December 31, 2026?

With several months remaining, expected Fed easing and potential growth slowdown support a chance of hitting the threshold, but sticky inflation, fiscal-term-premium pressure, and wide mortgage spreads keep the risk of staying above 5.70% substantial.

title: Bank of Canada Rate Hike in 2026?

forecast.rationale: The Bank of Canada is more likely to be in a hold-or-cut posture through 2026 if inflation remains near target and growth is subdued. A hike is still plausible if tariff-driven price pressures, wage persistence, or a renewed housing/credit upswing push inflation expectations higher, but this is a minority scenario.

title: Major U.S. bank bailout before 2027?

forecast.rationale: A major U.S. bank bailout is a low-frequency event, and after the 2023 banking stress regulators and banks have generally had time to improve liquidity planning and supervision. However, risks from commercial real estate losses, funding pressure, or a recession before end-2026 leave a meaningful tail risk of a large intervention.

title: Will Trump cut long term capital gains tax before 2027?

forecast.rationale: A long-term capital gains tax cut would likely require legislation and would be politically harder than extending the expiring TCJA individual tax provisions, because it is costly and highly skewed toward upper-income taxpayers. Trump and congressional Republicans may favor lower investment taxes, but competing fiscal constraints and higher-priority tax pledges make enactment before 2027 less likely than not.
